comment: Spotify going to 10.99 with still no lossless is a hard sell when Apple Music gives lossless and Spatial Audio in the same plan for basically the same money. Spotify Connect and the desktop app keep me here for now, but I'm not paying more for the same lossy audio.
Paying MORE for an app that hides my recently played behind a TikTok feed is insane. Bring back the old home screen or I'm done, I am seriously considering canceling my subscription.

Doesn't matter to me what they charge, I already cancelled. The renewal pop-up still shows up every time I open the app even after I unsubscribed, clearing cache and reinstalling did nothing. Anyone have a real fix?

Still worth it. Ad-free, offline downloads and casting for 10.99 is less than what I pay for my other subscriptions combined, and the free version is basically unusable. Annoying, but I'll keep paying.
Another price hike while the UI keeps getting worse and the recommendations keep going stale. If the app doesn't get better I'm moving to YouTube Music, the constant changes are getting old.
Raising the price while they keep taking features away? Liked songs still don't show on albums and I can't see my saved songs anywhere useful. Not worth the money, I'm going to unsubscribe again.
Price going up is fine if the features come with it, but I'd like exact play counts and radio that doesn't keep replaying songs I already know. I'll keep using stats.fm alongside it for now.
Paying more so my home screen can be full of podcasts I never play? I already cancelled my family plan over this UI and I can't even hide the podcasts permanently. Show me the music or don't bother.
They want 11 bucks a month and they still play ads in my podcasts? That's a joke. I already only pay for the music, and if this keeps getting shoved down my throat I'm switching to YouTube Premium.

Raising the price while the heart button is gone and the playlists can't be shared? Earnest question: why would I pay more for a worse playlist experience? I'm switching back to Apple Music, I might unsubscribe.
Paying more and still no lossless tier. Tidal's hi-fi is already included at a lower price, so why would I stay on Spotify for a worse product? Tidal all the way.
Shuffle still plays the same 20 songs from my 200-song playlist and now they want more money. Smart shuffle keeps adding songs I didn't ask for. I'm honestly looking at Apple Music again.
Don't care, I'm on the free tier anyway. The ads are tolerable as long as I can play what I want, and a price bump doesn't push me to Premium. Maybe I'll pay again someday.

Another price hike for a product that keeps breaking my playlists and adding songs I didn't ask for. Last time it was the missing features that made me leave, and nothing has changed since. Not paying more for that.
I keep auto-updates off for a reason, and I still don't want to pay more for an app I can't use the way I like. If the new layout is forced on me permanently I'm cancelling and staying cancelled.
Price going up on an app that still breaks after every update? Playback and offline downloads have been flaky for months and support hasn't fixed it. I'll be grumbling and keeping an old version.
Ugh, the student price is going from 4.99 to 5.99? That's a big percentage jump on a tight student budget. I'll keep the Hulu bundle, but if they go higher I'm going back to Apple Music.
They're raising prices on a plan that still doesn't have the features they removed. I track the votes and tests and none of the things I voted for are back. Price up for less is a hard pass for me.
Honestly $10.99 for the whole catalog is still a steal. Artists get paid pennies per stream, so a modest increase with more money going to the rights holders is fair. I'm staying.
Spotify raises its price again and the artists still get fractions of a cent per stream. Where does the extra money go? Not to the people making the music, that's for sure.

Absolutely hate this update and now I'm paying more for it? The music tab is a feed of cards and autoplay keeps playing stuff I didn't pick. If the new layout stays I'm switching to Apple Music, no question.

A dollar more for Premium is not the end of the world. It's still good bang for the buck for the catalog and ad-free listening, though I do worry about the free tier and whether quality keeps slipping.
Family plan going up a dollar is fine, we still split it a few bucks each and nobody in the house wants to go back to ads. Duo is still cheap per person. Worth it.
I can barely afford the 9.99 right now, so going up to 10.99 means I'm dropping back to the free version. Ad-free and skips are great but it's just not in the budget this month.
Prices going up a bit is fine with me. Discover Weekly and Release Radar still beat anything else for finding new artists, and the library is still huge. Keeping my Premium.

Price goes up and still no lossless tier, while Tidal and Apple already give hi-fi for less. I'll stay for Spotify Connect and the recommendations, but this is exactly the reason I mostly listen on Tidal.
